title: Consolidate socket IO queues and introduce lightweight span serializer to reduce CPU path copies
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: high tail-latency investigation showed disproportionate CPU time spent in request path serialization, repeated allocations, and frequent epoll/syscall handoffs from per-socket queues. This PR consolidates socket IO queue management into a small number of shared, per-NUMA event loops and replaces the heavy ad-hoc serializer with a lightweight span-based serializer to minimize copying and allocations. Approach: 1) Introduce io/event_loop_shard.{h,cc} that groups sockets by a fast hash (socket id -> shard) and processes batched readiness events using a batched epoll/poll loop. This reduces syscall frequency by coalescing readiness handling and amortizing lock acquisition across batches. 2) Replace the prior RequestMarshaller with SpanSerializer, a zero-allocation view-based serializer that composes IO frames by referencing buffer slices and only materializes a single contiguous frame when the network path requires it. SpanSerializer supports in-place KV-cache witness pointers so cached prefixes can be forwarded without copy. 3) Move blocking disk/metrics flushing out of the event loop into a bounded async worker pool with backpressure hooks; event loops now only run non-blocking tasks and lightweight admission control for continuous batching. 4) Scheduler changes: reduced size of the global CPU worker pool and enable local work-stealing between per-socket shards to reduce cross-thread wakeups; removed most explicit thread pinning in favor of shard affinity hints that let the OS schedule while preserving NUMA locality. 5) Compatibility: kept public API and RPC wire formats unchanged; added feature-flag to toggle SpanSerializer at runtime for staged rollout. Testing and validation: microbenchmarks show 18-28% reduction in median CPU cycles/request on our standard chat workload and 22% improvement in 95th percentile latency under synthetic burst traffic. End-to-end canary on staging for 72h with production-like queries (including embeddings and streaming) showed no increase in error rate and a 6% reduction in token-cost due to fewer retries. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in dedicated clusters for low-traffic customers, monitor per-route latency/cpu and KV-cache hit metrics in Console dashboards, then progressively enable for higher throughput pools. Caveats: the new event loop sharding introduces a small (<1%) CPU overhead for very low-concurrency single-connection scenarios due to batching window; also some kernel versions show different epoll semantics so we included a fallback to existing per-socket loop. Related work: builds on continuous-batching changes from ENG-3890 and addresses follow-ups from PRs that attempted to decouple serialization from affinity (see linked PRs). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for SpanSerializer and event loop shards - [x] Integration tests with KV cache and streaming enabled - [x] Performance regression tests added to benchmark-lab - [x] Feature-flag + rollout doc added in docs/ops/feature-flags.md
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial io shard scaffolding and tests; span serializer prototype; integrate span serializer into request path; cleanup, tests, and feature-flag wiring. Commits are small and focused with test coverage and perf harness additions.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice end-to-end numbers. Two things: can we avoid the extra memcpy when network driver already accepts scatter-gather? Consider adding an iovec path.
Aisha Patel: Good point — added an iovec fast-path in SpanSerializer and a test to verify zero-copy to sendmsg. See span_serializer.cc + tests.
Liang Chen: The worker_pool reduction looked risky for high core counts. Did you test with colocated workloads? I want to see results with mixed short/long sequences.

Aisha Patel: Ran mixed-load perf on perf-canary (2x cpu and 4x small/large sequences); results included in bench outputs show stable throughput and improved tail latency. Added notes to benchmark output directory.
Sofia Martinez: Please make sure the feature flag can be toggled per-cluster. Also add guard rails for kernel versions with known epoll behavioral differences.
Aisha Patel: Feature-flag is per-deployment and we added a kernel-version check with a documented fallback to the previous per-socket loop in event_loop_shard.cc.
ci_checks: CI: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), flake8/lint (pass), perf-smoke (pass), canary-deploy (pass on staging). One intermittent test (metrics/flush_test) was flaky and fixed in commit 4.
merge_summary: Merged via squash-merge after approvals from Miguel and Liang and green CI. No conflicts with main. Deployed to staging as feature-flag off; feature toggled on for canary clusters immediately after merge.
release_notes: Reduce CPU copies in request path by introducing SpanSerializer and consolidating socket IO into NUMA-aware event loop shards. Improves median CPU per request and tail latency for bursty traffic. Rollout behind a feature flag. See ENG-4121 for benchmarks and canary results.
notes_for_oncall: If increased request timeouts are observed after enabling the flag, check event_loop_shard metrics (batch_size, epoll_syscalls) and kv_cache prefix forwarding counters. Fallback: toggle feature-flag off to revert to previous marshaller and per-socket loops.
